cve_summary: Multiple stack-based buffer overflows in the iriap_getvaluebyclass_indication function in net/irda/iriap.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39 allow remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging connectivity to an IrDA infrared network and sending a large integer value for a (1) name length or (2) attribute length.
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Handles the retrieval of attribute values by class indication in the IRDA protocol.

Parameters: 
self (struct iriap_cb *): Pointer to the IRDA control block.
skb (struct sk_buff *): Pointer to the socket buffer containing the data.

Returns: 
None

Logic: The function begins by validating the input parameters and extracting the class name and attribute name from the socket buffer. It processes the names for lookup against the available objects and attributes. If the specified object or attribute is not found, it sends a response indicating the error. If both are found, it retrieves the attribute value and sends a successful response with the value. Debugging information is logged throughout the process to assist in tracing execution and errors.
"""

reference_missing_steps: strnlen-based validation of class and attribute names
candidate_missing_steps: explicit buffer length tracking and bounds-checked copies
judge_vs_vulnerable.rationale: Implementation 1 performs bounds checks on the input buffer by copying data into fixed-size buffers with explicit length tracking, and includes magic number validation. Implementation 2 performs null checks on input parameters and uses strnlen to validate the class and attribute names against the buffer length. Implementation 1 lacks explicit validation of the input buffer length and could overflow the fixed-size buffers if the input is malformed. Implementation 2 lacks magic number validation and explicit bounds checks on the input data before copying.

reference_missing_steps: strnlen-based validation of class and attribute names
explicit error logging for invalid names
candidate_missing_steps: bounds check on name_len before memcpy
bounds check on attr_len before memcpy
judge_vs_fixed.rationale: Implementation 1 performs explicit length checks on the class and attribute names before copying them into fixed-size buffers, ensuring they do not overflow. It also includes assertions for input validation and object/attribute existence checks. Implementation 2 uses strnlen and pointer arithmetic to extract names from the buffer, but does not perform explicit bounds checks on the names before use, relying on the structure of the input. It also includes error checks for object and attribute existence but lacks explicit buffer overflow protections for the names.
